+assignees:

+title: 'Add tests for RunScript: generatedContent, not-under-scripts corrective, confinement corrective'
+---
+`Sources/FoundationModelsSkills/Resources/RunScript.swift`
+
+Coverage: 85.7% (60/70 lines)
+
+Uncovered lines: 116-120, 150, 153, 182-184
+
+Add these tests. Do not change `RunScript.swift`.
+
+1. Lines 116-120 -- `public var generatedContent: GeneratedContent`.
+   The CLI driver uses this property to encode the operation back to the
+   model-facing payload. No test reads it. Make a `RunScript`, read
+   `generatedContent`, then decode it again with `init(_ content:)`. Make
+   sure the round trip keeps `id`, `path`, `arguments` and `timeout`. Do
+   the test two times: one time with `arguments` and `timeout` set, one
+   time with both `nil`. With both `nil`, make sure the payload does not
+   hold the `arguments` and `timeout` keys.
+
+2. Lines 150, 182-184 -- `notUnderScriptsMessage(path:)`.
+   `execute(in:)` refuses a path that does not start with
+   `scriptsDirectoryPrefix`. Run a script whose `path` is `hello.sh` at
+   the skill root, not under `scripts/`. Enable script execution in the
+   registry policy, and grant the script through `allowed-tools`, so the
+   test reaches this guard. Make sure the result is `.corrective(_:)` and
+   that the message reads "The path `hello.sh` is not runnable: `run
+   script` only executes files under `scripts/`."
+
+3. Line 153 -- `PathConfinement.deniedMessage(path:)` inside `execute(in:)`.
+   The guard runs for a path that starts with `scripts/` but escapes the
+   skill directory. Use `scripts/../../outside.sh`. Make sure the result
+   is the confinement corrective, not the not-under-scripts one. This
+   test proves the order of the two guards.
+
+Put the tests in `Tests/FoundationModelsSkillsTests/`, next to the tests
+that are there for this operation. #coverage-gap
\ No newline at end of file
